definitions.explanation: dishes served alongside rice in a Japanese meal; anything eaten with rice as the main accompaniment

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}のおかずは{何|なに}？
おかずを{作|つく}り{過|す}ぎた。
examples.english: I made too many side dishes.

examples.japanese: このおかずはご{飯|はん}が{進|すす}む。
examples.english: This side dish goes really well with rice.

notes:
KANJI:
Can be written as {御菜|おかず} or {御数|おかず}, but hiragana is most common.

JAPANESE MEAL STRUCTURE:
A traditional Japanese meal consists of:
- ご{飯|はん} (rice) - the main staple
- {汁|しる}{物|もの} (soup, e.g., {味噌汁|みそしる})
- おかず (side dishes) - the accompaniments

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ご{飯|はん}のおかず (side dish for rice)
- おかずになる (to serve as a side dish)
- {今日|きょう}のおかず (today's side dish)

RELATED:
- {惣菜|そうざい} (prepared dishes, deli food)
- {副菜|ふくさい} (side dish - formal)
- {主菜|しゅさい} (main dish)
